The body called Ibadi Islam 'the majority faith of Oman'. Oman publishes no religious statistics; the Library of Congress country study (1993) calls Ibadis the majority, while recent estimates (cited on Wikipedia from the US State Department) put Ibadis and Sunnis at about 45 % each. The body now says Oman is Ibadism's main home, gives both views (as of 2026), and adds that elected Ibadi imams ruled Oman's interior until the 1950s; the notes explain the contested figure.
